questions.question: To prevent a rollover, a driver should:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly. Keep your cargo low and close to the ground. This lowers the vehicle's center of gravity and helps prevent rollovers.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, match the colors. Service lines are often:
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, connect matching colors. Service lines are usually blue. Emergency lines are usually red. Color coding helps you avoid mistakes.

questions.question: Starting in which year were newly manufactured trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance may be difficult to drive:
questions.explanation: Trailers with low clearance are hard to drive over railroad crossings. Raised crossings can be especially challenging, especially for low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers.

questions.question: The easiest way to know your trailer is skidding is to:

options.text: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left the lane.
Release the brake pedal and then push it down again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left the lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is still in its proper position.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need extra space on the road because they:

options.text: Drive more slowly than other commercial motor vehicles.
Are heavier than other commercial motor vehicles.
Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Manage space carefully when driving combination vehicles.

questions.question: If you drive a vehicle built before 1998 and are unsure if it has ABS, you can:

options.text: Check for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: For vehicles built before 1998, check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes to see if it has Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Place the trailer air supply control in "emergency" position to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start driving. After the trailer rolls freely, pull out the trailer air supply control or place it in "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle turns a corner:

options.text: The turn should be made as tightly as possible.
The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is acceptable for street signs to be knocked over if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. It is especially strong on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, the driver should:

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel in one direction, then in the other.

questions.explanation: If your trailer skids, release the brakes. The wheels will grip the road again and the trailer will straighten out.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The trailer detaches from the tractor.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost, the emergency brakes will turn on.

questions.question: What happens to your brakes if oil and water build up in the air tanks?
questions.explanation: Drain your air tanks daily to remove water and oil. If these build up, they can damage your brakes and make them work poorly.

questions.question: What should you do if your trailer starts to skid?
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This lets the wheels grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out.

questions.question: How should you brake in a tractor-trailer with ABS?

options.text: Use extra force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you normally would.
questions.explanation: With ABS, brake the same way you would in any other vehicle. Do not change your braking technique.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, how should the tractor be positioned?

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up to couple. Backing at an angle can damage the landing gear.

questions.question: When are rollovers most likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Slow down before entering turns and curves, especially with a full load.

questions.question: Older trailers without spring brakes will have no brakes if the air supply leaks away. What happens?

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks, there will be no brakes and the wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: It is located on the front of a trailer.
It is located on the instrument panel.
It stops air from escaping the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from escaping the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control airflow between trailers. Keep the rear shut-off valve closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer will usually continue straight.
The trailer will likely swing around.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will likely swing around.
questions.explanation: When trailer wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing around, which can cause a jackknife.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Get out of the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services for help.
